notes: Switzerland Hardening I (border cash) + Hardening II (accounts/AML/residency evidence). H1 authorities FOCBS + SR 631.052 preserved unchanged. H2 appends AMLA SR 955.0, AMLO-FINMA SR 955.033, FINMA AML supervision, CDB 20, FINMA high-risk-client dossier, and temporal 2026/2027 sources. As of 2026-09-09: current AMLA consolidation Status as of 1 March 2024 remains in force; revised AMLA/LETA enter into force 1 October 2026 (future). AMLO-FINMA Stand 1 January 2023 is current; FINMA launched AMLO-FINMA partial-revision consultation on 12 May 2026 with industry expectation of 1 January 2027 effectiveness (future). CDB 20 (13 June 2018 / in force 1 January 2020) remains the current bank due-diligence framework on 2026-09-09. No general resident/non-resident statutory account entitlement or prior-approval rule is established in this pack. Does not modify claims.json, bindings, adoption, M2.5, or data/rules/switzerland.json.

source_conflicts.topic: CHF 10,000 operator wording on FOCBS page vs ordinance
source_conflicts.detail: FOCBS English page body uses 'CHF 10,000 or more' / 'equals or exceeds CHF 10,000' for inquiry and information-system registration. Ordinance Art. 3 uses 'mindestens 10 000 Franken' (at least CHF 10,000 / >=). A FOCBS page lead sentence also uses 'over 10,000 francs' shorthand. Disposition: prefer the body inquiry/registration clauses and Art. 3 'mindestens' (>=) for Hardening I candidates; do not promote a strict-exceeding (>) operator for the threshold mechanics.
source_conflicts.wording_boundary: Use >= / CHF 10,000 or more / equals or exceeds / mindestens 10 000 Franken. Do not flatten to > CHF 10,000 for the inquiry or registration mechanics.

source_conflicts.topic: public >=CHF10k registration narrative vs Art. 6 reporting independence
source_conflicts.detail: FOCBS public guidance states that if cash equals or exceeds CHF 10,000, an entry is registered in the FOCBS information system. Ordinance Art. 6 Abs. 2 states that customs reporting (Meldung) to the Oberzolldirektion is permissible independent of the cash amount. Disposition: keep FOCBS public >=10k registration as a distinct public-guidance proposition; keep Art. 6 amount-independent reporting as a distinct statutory reporting permission. Do not collapse them into one threshold-only recording rule.
source_conflicts.wording_boundary: FOCBS public surface: >= CHF 10,000 information-system entry. Ordinance Art. 6: Meldung may occur independent of amount.

source_conflicts.topic: current AMLA consolidation vs revised AMLA effective 1 October 2026
source_conflicts.detail: On 2026-09-09 the Fedlex AMLA consolidation (Status as of 1 March 2024) is the operative current text. The Federal Council has set 1 October 2026 as entry into force for the revised AMLA and transparency-register act. Disposition: H2 current candidates use only the pre-1-Oct-2026 operative AMLA; 1 Oct 2026 reforms are temporal/future only.
source_conflicts.wording_boundary: Do not draft 1 October 2026 AMLA reforms as current account/AML rules before that date.

source_conflicts.topic: current AMLO-FINMA vs 2026 consultation / expected 2027 revision
source_conflicts.detail: Current AMLO-FINMA Stand 1 January 2023 remains operative on 2026-09-09. FINMA consultation of 12 May 2026 on partial revision is not yet current law; expected effectiveness commonly stated as 1 January 2027 alongside revised CDB. Disposition: keep current ordinance and CDB 20 for present drafting; record 2027 package as future only.
source_conflicts.wording_boundary: Do not apply consulted/future AMLO-FINMA or successor CDB as current rules.

missing_authorities.topic: general statutory right of residents/non-residents to open Swiss bank or FCY accounts
missing_authorities.search_record: Bounded search 2026-09-09 across Fedlex AMLA SR 955.0 (Arts. 1–11 operative due-diligence/reporting), FINMA Combating money laundering page, CDB 20 Arts. 1–28 account-opening due diligence, FINMA high-risk-client dossier. Result: AML/onboarding duties and institutional risk-tolerance expectations found; no federal provision establishing a general legal entitlement for residents or non-residents to open or maintain bank or foreign-currency accounts. Market practice of Swiss banks offering accounts is not treated as entitlement evidence.
missing_authorities.wording_boundary: Do not draft 'Swiss residents/non-residents may open accounts' or 'freely' as a statutory entitlement from H2 evidence.

missing_authorities.topic: general SNB/FINMA/federal prior approval for ordinary account opening
missing_authorities.search_record: Bounded search 2026-09-09 of AMLA Arts. 1–11, FINMA AML supervision page, CDB 20 account-opening articles, Federal Council AML communications for H2. No general prior approval by SNB, FINMA, or another federal authority for ordinary resident/non-resident account opening was located. Absence of an established general prior-approval requirement is recorded as not_established for a broad negative claim; bank acceptance and AML onboarding are not government approval. Do not candidate-extract 'without prior approval' or 'no approval is ever required'.
missing_authorities.wording_boundary: If later bounded, phrase only as 'general prior approval by [named authority] not established for ordinary account opening' — never 'unrestricted account access'.

missing_authorities.topic: AMLA/CDB residence-based account entitlement or prohibition class
missing_authorities.search_record: Bounded search of AMLA due-diligence articles and CDB 20 identification/controlling-person/beneficial-owner rules for explicit resident vs non-resident account-opening categories, general prohibitions, or general approval requirements keyed to residence. No such general residence-based entitlement/prohibition/approval class located in the reviewed federal AML / bank due-diligence corpus. Residence may appear as domicile/address data or within risk assessment; that does not create a statutory resident/non-resident account class. Do not infer identical treatment in every regime.
missing_authorities.wording_boundary: Do not equate non-resident with high-risk client; do not invent residence-based account rights or bans from silence.

sources.label: Federal Office for Customs and Border Security (FOCBS) — Cash, foreign currency and securities
sources.authority: Federal Office for Customs and Border Security (FOCBS / BAZG)
sources.notes: Current FOCBS English traveller guidance for notes/coins, foreign currencies and bearer negotiable instruments. Establishes unrestricted carriage into/through/out of Switzerland, no spontaneous FOCBS declaration duty, information-on-request during checks, >= CHF 10,000 inquiry and registration mechanics, refusal/false-information consequences, and temporary seizure on ML/TF suspicion.

sources.label: SR 631.052 — Verordnung über die Kontrolle des grenzüberschreitenden Barmittelverkehrs (11 February 2009; Stand 1 January 2022)
sources.notes: Official Fedlex consolidated German text of the Ordinance on the control of cross-border cash movements. FOCBS identifies this instrument as the legal basis for cross-border cash controls. English ELI path does not supply a separate authoritative English text; excerpts use faithful translation from German. Stand am 1. Januar 2022.

sources.label: SR 955.0 — Federal Act on Combating Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing in the Financial Sector (Anti-Money Laundering Act, AMLA / GwG)
sources.notes: Official Fedlex English consolidation; page declares text in force; Status as of 1 March 2024. Operative on 2026-09-09. Revised AMLA package enters into force 1 October 2026 (see SRC-CH-FC-AMLA-EIF-2026) and must not be applied as current. Primary legal spine for financial-intermediary due diligence: Arts. 3–8 identity, beneficial owner, repetition, special due diligence, records/update, organisational measures; Art. 9 reporting. Does not establish account-opening entitlement.

sources.label: SR 955.033 — FINMA Anti-Money Laundering Ordinance (AMLO-FINMA / GwV-FINMA)
sources.authority: Swiss Financial Market Supervisory Authority FINMA / Fedlex
sources.notes: Current Fedlex consolidation Stand am 1. Januar 2023. Implements AMLA for FINMA-supervised intermediaries. H2 uses this primarily for temporal/current-status pinning; detailed article candidates prefer AMLA statutory text and FINMA supervisory summaries where sufficient. Partial revision consultation launched 12 May 2026; expected future effectiveness 1 January 2027 (see SRC-CH-FINMA-AMLO-CONSULT-2026) — do not apply as current.

sources.label: FINMA — Combating money laundering in the context of financial market supervision
sources.authority: Swiss Financial Market Supervisory Authority FINMA
sources.notes: Current FINMA supervisory overview of AMLA due-diligence/disclosure requirements and CDB 20 recognition for banks/securities firms. Supervisory corroboration — does not replace AMLA statutory wording for legal scope.

sources.label: Agreement on the Swiss banks’ code of conduct with regard to the exercise of due diligence (CDB 20)
sources.notes: English CDB 20 text (SBA agreement of 13 June 2018; in force 1 January 2020). FINMA AML page confirms FINMA approval and bank/securities-firm application for contracting-partner identity and beneficial-owner identification; also applies to certain CISA institutions for those duties. Scope limited to banks/securities dealers (and specified CISA subjects) — not all financial intermediaries. Remains current bank due-diligence framework on 2026-09-09 pending future CDB revision timed with AMLO-FINMA 2027 package. Does not prove statutory account entitlement, unrestricted transfers, or absence of exchange controls. URL is a published English PDF copy of the SBA instrument used for verbatim capture.

sources.label: FINMA — Focus on high-risk clients in the context of combating money laundering (2024)
sources.authority: Swiss Financial Market Supervisory Authority FINMA
sources.notes: FINMA dossier extract from Annual Report 2024 on risk tolerance, high-risk clients/countries/services outside tolerance, source-of-assets clarification for high-risk relationships, and careful monitoring of higher-risk transactions. Institutional risk-acceptance evidence — not a residence-based legal class and not a universal entitlement negation beyond risk-tolerance boundary.

sources.label: Federal Council — New anti-money laundering rules entry into force (12 June 2026)
sources.authority: Swiss Federal Council / State Secretariat for International Finance
sources.notes: Temporal authority: revised AMLA and Act on Transparency of Legal Persons / beneficial owners enter into force 1 October 2026. On 2026-09-09 these reforms are enacted-but-not-yet-effective — future relative to H2 current drafting. Do not apply as current account/AML rules.

sources.label: FINMA — Consultation on partial revision of AMLO-FINMA (12 May 2026)
sources.authority: Swiss Financial Market Supervisory Authority FINMA
sources.notes: Temporal: FINMA launched AMLO-FINMA partial-revision consultation 12 May 2026 (to 9 June 2026). Industry/official commentary expects effectiveness around 1 January 2027 with revised CDB. Consultation text is not current law. Keep current vs future explicit.
